headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can feed Superset outputs into shared pipelines, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error exposure without direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, but Airflow can orchestrate files/APIs and Superset consumes APIs, so a manual or workspace bridge could let attacker-controlled content influence downstream interpretation. The pair lacks direct evidence of automatic ingestion, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks write content that Superset later ingests as trusted text or SQL
IF an operator bridges the two via shared files, clipboard, or a shared API payload
mitigations: Use a separate staging folder for any Airflow-to-Superset handoff
Add a review step before Superset ingests Airflow-produced text
Strip instructions/markup from exported content
Disable any automatic import path between the two
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no data classes touched and no secrets handled, so there is no direct sensitive-data flow. A broad-egress Airflow instance and allowlisted-egress Superset could still leak if operators place sensitive files in a shared workspace, but that requires extra setup and the blast radius is limited by the absent data classes.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files
IF either agent is configured to transmit file contents through its network egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Use separate service accounts and credentials
Review outbound destinations for both agents
Rotate any credentials stored near the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Superset has allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, OAuth scopes, or elevated privileges. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only limited overlap on external API use is visible, so the conflict risk is low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or database
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials
Avoid shared mutable targets
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for overlapping scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow commonly produces pipeline outputs that Superset can visualize or consume, so B may treat A's artifacts as authoritative if no verification step exists. The pair has no direct evidence of such a pipeline, but the interaction is plausible in default data-engineering workflows, making medium the safer choice.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or queries are built directly from Airflow-produced outputs
IF no validation step checks Airflow artifacts before Superset uses them
mitigations: Add schema validation before handoff
Require human review for generated metrics
Compare outputs against source-of-truth tables
Log and alert on unexpected value shifts
requires-engineering: implement signed artifact verification

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile, and both touch no data classes. With no compliance-relevant flow shown, there is no plausible pairwise compliance breach to score above none.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF one agent is configured with stricter retention or residency rules than the other
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Review retention settings before deployment
Keep regulated data out of the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
